name: Gong Sheng
current_role: Standing Executive Director and President, Jiangsu Shagang Group (Zhangjiagang)
profile: Gong Sheng is the long-serving president of Jiangsu Shagang Group, China's largest private steelmaker (about 40m tonnes of crude steel in 2023). He took over as president from founder Shen Wenrong in 2011, after serving as vice president, and holds a shareholding in the group. He still runs operations under chairman Shen Bin.
interesting_fact: He succeeded founder Shen Wenrong as Shagang's president in 2011 and has run day-to-day operations of China's biggest private steelmaker for more than a decade.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2026 he personally led a site visit to Shagang's Huaigang special-steel subsidiary, which reflects his hands-on, plant-floor management style.
notes: Low public profile, and there is almost no personal biography online. The best route is the Shagang Group board office (集团董事局 常委办公室) email. Listed arm: Jiangsu Shagang Co (002075.SZ).

name: Chen Qiming
current_role: Shareholder associated with SF Express / SF Holding (002352.SZ); no executive title found
profile: Chen Qiming is one of nine SF Express-linked individuals on the 2020 Hurun Global/China Rich List, with an estimated RMB 3.1bn (rank 1,705). The listing implies an early or indirect stake in SF Holding, the delivery giant founded by Wang Wei. I found no published biography or SF board or management role.
interesting_fact: He was one of nine SF-linked people on the 2020 Hurun list, a year in which SF's rising share price added five new SF billionaires-by-yuan.
notes: He is not among SF Holding's directors, supervisors or senior management in the filings I checked. He is probably an early partner or indirect shareholder. Identity details are thin. The only route is via SF Holding IR, which may not forward.

name: Sudhir Valia
current_role: Former director of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries; retired from the board at the 2025 AGM. Private investor and businessman.
profile: Sudhir V. Valia is a Mumbai chartered accountant and the brother-in-law of Sun Pharma founder Dilip Shanghvi. He is part of Sun Pharma's promoter group and held about 0.6% of the company in 2025. He was whole-time director from 2005 to 2019, running finance, commercial, operations, projects and quality control, then served as a non-executive director until he chose not to seek re-election in 2025.
interesting_fact: As Sun Pharma's whole-time director from February 2005, he oversaw finance, operations, projects and quality control during the decade it grew into India's largest drugmaker. He also sat on the board of Taro Pharmaceutical (Israel) from 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chartered accountant (B.Com, University of Mumbai) and built more than four decades of taxation and finance experience before becoming the finance architect behind his brother-in-law's pharma group.
notes: He left the Sun Pharma board at the 2025 AGM, so a Sun Pharma contact is a weak route. He has no public social media. In 2019 he moved to a non-executive role after whistleblower complaints about loans to firms linked to him, so avoid that topic. Keep any approach low-key.

name: Li Lei
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2018-19) and vice chairman of Qutoutiao Inc.; no current public role found
profile: Li Lei co-founded Qutoutiao, the Shanghai 'pay-to-read' news-aggregator app, with Eric Tan Sixiao. He served as CEO from August 2018, when it listed on Nasdaq, until May 2019, and then as vice chairman. He held about 7.6% of the company (15.6% of the votes) in 2022, before Qutoutiao was delisted in 2023.
interesting_fact: He led Qutoutiao through its September 2018 Nasdaq IPO, which came about two years after launch. The app grew fast by paying users in coins to read and share articles, aimed at lower-tier cities.
deep_cut_fact: He studied while building the business, earning an associate degree in law (2014) and a bachelor's in law (2017) from the Open University of China. Earlier he was director of advertising solutions at Shanda's ad subsidiary, Shanghai Shengyue (2010-13).
notes: Qutoutiao was delisted from Nasdaq in 2023, and I found no current company or personal contact. He is low-profile since stepping down as CEO in 2019. Don't confuse him with other people named Li Lei (e.g. former ByteDance AI Lab head Lei Li).
